What is the global environment for?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. Global selection is the fallback for files outside workspace folders, not a mirror of each project's environment. Your Hatch extension should not need to overwrite it whenever a project selection changes: consumers should use the Python Environments API's `onDidChangeEnvironment` and `getEnvironment(uri)` for scoped selections. The maintainer's explanation at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1491#issuecomment-4383115486 recommends supporting both APIs and preferring Python Environments when available. Closing this as an answered API question. For further support questions, please use https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/discussions/categories/q-a.

About python projects feature
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. The current extension treats every workspace root as a Python project, regardless of its contents, as documented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/blob/main/docs/managing-python-projects.md. Workspace roots also cannot currently be removed through the Remove Python Project action. This leaves a product question for mixed-language workspaces: should every root remain an environment-association container, or should non-Python roots be excluded or removable? Keeping this open to settle that behavior and make the documentation consistent.

rows.title: Automated terminal activation kills all running tasks in terminals
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and for confirming the workaround. Command-based activation is intentionally the default because it can activate environments in any shell; `shellStartup` is the non-disruptive opt-in for supported shells, and `off` is available where no automatic activation is wanted. The same Ctrl+C behavior was subsequently reviewed and closed as designed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1570. Please continue using `"python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType": "shellStartup"` for this workflow.

rows.title: IndentationError when executing nested for-loops via “Run Selection/Line in Python Terminal”
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. That command is implemented by the core Python extension, so consolidating there will keep the investigation with the owning code; this report adds useful evidence that nested loops fail both line-by-line and cell-by-cell.
